newsitem.title: UK: LME People - Bagri ennobled in UK Honours List.
newsitem.headline: LME People - Bagri ennobled in UK Honours List.

text.p: Raj Bagri, Chairman of the London Metal Exchange (LME), has been made a life peer in Britain's New Year's Honours List, the highest award given to the business community.
Bagri has been chairman of the world's largest non-ferrous metals exchange since 1993. He was not immediately available for comment.
His peerage comes against the background of the LME's most turbulent year since the 1985 collapse of the tin price, with the market rocked by the Sumitomo Corp scandal in June.

The Japanese metals conglomerate fired its head copper trader, Yasuo Hamanaka, alleging he had admitted running up losses of $2.6 billion in unauthorised copper trading. In the aftermath of the affair, Bagri vigorously defended the LME's role, saying at October's annual LME dinner that the Exchange had helped expose the Hamanaka problem.
The LME also asked Britain's top markets regulator, the Securities and Investments Board (SIB), to review the market.
Earlier this month, SIB recommended that the LME review some of its rules and executive functions, but a wide-ranging report largely endorsed the market's practices.
The peerage recognised the contribution of Bagri, born in India, to Britain as a leading member of the Asian community.
Bagri, 66, started work as a filing clerk in a Calcutta metals business in 1945. He now owns and runs the multinational Metdist Group of companies with annual turnover of around 500 million stg.
He has been associated with the LME since 1970, when Metdist Trading Ltd was incorporated, becoming a member of the Exchange's old Management Committee in 1973.
In 1983, he became a Director of the Metal Market and Exchange Company - forerunner of the LME's present Board. Bagri became Board vice-chairman in 1990.

Since he became chairman in January 1993, the LME has continued to grow, with trading volumes higher and the exchange warehousing system expanded worldwide, most notably in the U.S. where warehouses for storing copper were introduced in 1995.
Bagri was re-elected LME chairman at the Exchange's December Board meeting.
